title: "diag() on a single value builds an identity matrix of that size"
ref: LEN-12
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'dim(diag(c(4)))'
reponse: '4 4'
attendu: "`1 1`, a one-by-one matrix holding 4"
versions: "All"
source: "hadley/strict"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
variances <- c(4, 9)
diag(variances)
variances <- c(4)
diag(variances)
```
:::

## Why

`diag()` has two behaviours. Given a vector of several values, it puts them on the diagonal of a square matrix. Given a single number, it takes it as a size and returns the identity matrix of that size, truncated to an integer: `diag(2.7)` is a 2 by 2 identity, `diag(0.5)` a 0 by 0 matrix.

A function that builds a covariance matrix from a vector of variances therefore works until the day the vector holds a single value. It then returns a 4 by 4 identity, with no warning.

## The remedy

Give the size explicitly with `nrow`: the result is the expected diagonal matrix whatever the length of the vector.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
diag(variances, nrow = length(variances))
```
:::
